tweets.text:
One example task comes from Mock Service Worker, a JavaScript library for mocking network requests. The task asks the model to fix a user-reported bug: resetHandlers() doesn’t restart the generator.

Claude Opus 5.5 fixes the bug by discarding the old generator reference upon reset, so the next request starts a new one. That solves the reported bug, but dropping the reference to the generator means that any cleanup code the user already had in a finally block will never run.

The prompt doesn’t mention cleanup, but an experienced JavaScript developer knows to expect finally to run when a generator is abandoned, and Opus 5.5’s solution fails to satisfy that implicit correctness expectation.

FrontierCode 2.0 separates model tiers more clearly than FrontierCode 1.1. It also ranks them differently: on DeepSWE v1.1, Muse Wonder 1.0 and Gemini 4 Argon score highest, but on FrontierCode 2.0 they land in the middle of the pack. https://t.co/ql8EupPGxJ
